passage:
Dear Mr. Sterling,

The decision to host our wedding reception at The Grandview Hotel was based on your reputation for "flawless execution" and "uncompromising luxury." Unfortunately, the experience my wife and I endured last Saturday was characterized by systemic technical failures and a disregard for our specific catering requirements, transforming what should have been a seamless celebration into a series of stressful logistical hurdles.

Our primary grievance involves the complete failure of the audiovisual system during the keynote speeches. Despite having conducted a successful soundcheck with your on-site technician at 2:00 PM, the microphones ceased functioning entirely the moment my father-in-law stood up to speak. For forty-five minutes, our 150 guests sat in awkward silence while your staff scrambled to find a replacement amplifier. This was not a minor glitch; it was a total breakdown that effectively severed the emotional core of our evening. The speeches, which we had planned for months, were eventually delivered to a restless, distracted room without any amplification.

The disappointment continued with the dinner service. We had been very clear during our final tasting regarding the "Shellfish-Free" status of Table 12, where three of our immediate family members with severe allergies were seated. To our horror, the "Artisan Seafood Risotto" served to that table contained prominent pieces of lobster. Had my sister not noticed before taking a bite, the evening would have likely ended in a medical emergency rather than a toast. Furthermore, the main course for the general guest list was served nearly ninety minutes behind schedule, resulting in several elderly guests departing before the cake was even cut.

We invested over $22,000 in this event, trusting that the "Premium Wedding Package" covered the expertise required to manage these details. The lack of oversight from your floor manager, who was nowhere to be found during the AV crisis, is unacceptable for a venue of your caliber. While we cannot recreate the moment, we expect a significant financial adjustment to reflect the diminished value of the services provided. Specifically, I am requesting a full refund of the $3,500 service fee and a 20% rebate on the total catering invoice.

I look forward to your prompt proposal on how you intend to rectify this situation.

Sincerely,
Jonathan Miller
